seoTitle: How to Combine 2 Charts in TradingView Easily
metaDescription: Learn how to combine two symbols into one TradingView chart window, overlay them, and adjust scales and colors for clear price comparison.
intro: Combining two charts into a single TradingView window makes it easy to compare stocks, indices, or crypto pairs without switching between tabs. This guide shows how to overlay a second symbol, adjust the visual settings, and read the comparison clearly.

steps.heading: Open your first chart
steps.body: Start with the primary symbol you want as the base of your comparison.

steps.heading: Overlay the second symbol
steps.body: Use TradingView's Compare feature to add a second symbol directly onto the same chart window instead of opening a separate one.

steps.heading: Compare price movements visually
steps.body: With both symbols overlaid, watch how their price lines move relative to each other over the selected timeframe.

steps.heading: Adjust scales and colors
steps.body: Switch to percentage scale if the two symbols trade at very different price levels, and assign distinct colors so each line is easy to follow.

steps.heading: Apply it to your use case
steps.body: Use this combined view for comparing a stock against its index, two competing companies, or related crypto pairs to gauge relative performance.

faq.question: What's the easiest way to combine two charts in TradingView?
faq.answer: The Compare tool is the simplest method — it overlays a second symbol directly onto your existing chart without opening a new window.

faq.question: Can I combine a stock and a crypto chart together?
faq.answer: Yes, TradingView's Compare feature works across asset classes, so you can overlay a stock against a crypto pair or index.

faq.question: Why do the two lines look mismatched in scale?
faq.answer: This happens when the two symbols trade at very different price levels — switching to percentage scale usually fixes the visual mismatch.

faq.question: Is this feature available on the free TradingView plan?
faq.answer: Yes, basic chart overlay and comparison is available on TradingView's free plan.
